name: Strait of Gibraltar
note: Only 13 km wide at its narrowest; ships have crossed here since antiquity.
description: The Strait of Gibraltar is the Mediterranean's only natural door. Between the Rock of Gibraltar on the European shore and the mountains of Morocco on the African one, the strait narrows to about thirteen kilometres — close enough that each continent is plainly visible from the other. Everything the Mediterranean exchanges with the Atlantic by sea passes here, as it has since antiquity, when the twin headlands were known as the Pillars of Hercules and marked, for a time, the edge of the known world. The strait has been a frontier and a crossing in equal measure: Tariq ibn Ziyad's army crossed north in 711, Nelson's fleet fought off Cape Trafalgar just outside it in 1805, and today it carries one of the densest concentrations of shipping in the world, watched from both shores.
